subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should Telegram first-run setup replace default pairing with token-verified owner allowlist capture, use a post-bootstrap owner-derived default flip, or preserve pairing as the default with stronger manual allowlist guidance?
rationale: The request changes who becomes trusted during Telegram first-run setup and affects existing default authorization semantics, so automation cannot choose the security boundary safely without maintainer intent.

options.title: Token-Verified Owner Capture
options.body: Generate a short setup token, require the intended owner to send it to the bot, then write dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom for that numeric Telegram ID while preserving explicit pairing configs.

options.title: Post-Bootstrap Default Flip
options.body: Keep first-run pairing unchanged, then derive allowlist behavior from commands.ownerAllowFrom after the first approved owner as tracked by the broader cross-channel issue.

options.title: Keep Pairing Default
options.body: Leave runtime/setup defaults as pairing and improve warning, doctor, and docs guidance for users who want owner-only allowlist mode.

recommendation.title: Token-Verified Owner Capture
recommendation.body: Generate a short setup token, require the intended owner to send it to the bot, then write dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom for that numeric Telegram ID while preserving explicit pairing configs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current code-history signal across Telegram setup, config defaults, runtime fallback, and prior review context.
